{"selected_source_ids":["D01","D02","D03","D04","D05","D07","D08","D09","D10","D11","D13","D14","D15","D16","D19"],"excluded_sources":[{"source_id":"D06","reason":"task_irrelevant"},{"source_id":"D12","reason":"task_irrelevant"},{"source_id":"D17","reason":"task_irrelevant"},{"source_id":"D18","reason":"task_irrelevant"},{"source_id":"D20","reason":"task_irrelevant"}],"selection_rationale":"The review task focuses on how batch adsorption information (equilibrium capacities, kinetics) translates—or fails to translate—to continuous treatment performance (columns, RSSCTs, pilot, and full-scale), and what minimum evidence is needed for defensible service-life or scale-up claims.

I selected primary studies that:
- report PFAS adsorption in fixed-bed/RSSCT/pilot/full-scale systems and/or explicitly connect batch tests to column-scale performance;
- provide quantitative breakthrough metrics (e.g., BV10/BV50, media life, EBCT/contact time) or modeling of breakthrough relevant to service-life prediction; and/or
- examine the influence of flow, contact time, water quality, competing constituents, and PFAS mixtures on adsorption performance and breakthrough.

Excluded documents either focus on subsurface fate or air–water interfacial adsorption (not water-treatment adsorption scaling), on non-adsorptive technologies (e.g., foam fractionation, membranes without column adsorbents), or on batch equilibrium in complex AFFF matrices without any column, breakthrough, or scale-up content.

Summary by source:
- D01 (pilot AER resins, breakthrough, Thomas modeling, comparison with batch data, EBCT and bed volumes, media usage rates): directly informs how batch adsorption relates to pilot column performance and media life; strongly relevant to all components.
- D02 (GAC batch, RSSCT, and full-scale-type adsorbers, correlations and alternative methods for breakthrough prediction): directly compares batch, RSSCT, and fixed-bed behavior, and discusses when each can be used for predicting performance.
- D03 (PFAS adsorption to GAC, multicomponent modeling, competition, IAST limitations under realistic mixtures and source water conditions): provides quantitative evidence on how PFAS mixtures and competing species affect capacities and the reliability of batch-based models.
- D04 (GAC and IX columns in PFAS-impacted groundwaters, RSSCT design to simulate pilot/full-scale, influence of EBCT and competing adsorbates): central for translating short tests to long-term performance in realistic waters and examining water-quality effects.
- D05 (RSSCT vs pilot-scale performance for multiple groundwaters, DOC impacts, Thomas modeling, comparison of predicted vs observed breakthrough and media life): directly addresses scale-up and service-life prediction.
- D07 (GAC RSSCTs in groundwater, discussion of limitations of isotherm-only approaches, design of RSSCTs, EBCT and chromatographic effects, short vs long chain PFAS breakthrough): links batch concepts, RSSCT design, and breakthrough behavior.
- D08 (Biochar and GAC sorption including batch kinetics, equilibrium, and diffusion-limited transport modeling to predict bed volumes to breakthrough): provides a clear case of using batch-derived parameters and transport modeling to estimate column performance, along with noted limitations.
- D09 (RSSCT-based comparison of multiple adsorbents and waters, development of an adsorbent use-rate/cost framework, challenges of comparing breakthrough across conditions): informs how to compare media performance and what metrics are required for defensible treatment selection.
- D10 (β-cyclodextrin adsorbent, batch vs column behavior across contact times, Thomas fits, BV50 dependence on CT, mixture effects): directly compares kinetic parameters from batch to columns and shows when batch fails to predict continuous performance.
- D11 (NF + GAC/IX RSSCTs for wastewater effluent and NF permeate, effect of pretreatment and matrix on BV10 and performance improvement factors): shows how matrix removal and co-contaminants alter fixed-bed service life and highlights the importance of influent quality.
- D13 (model adaptations for competitive PFAS breakthrough curves in GAC, media service-life prediction, desorption modeling, composite hazard index-based media-life assessment): provides explicit methodology and evidence on how breakthrough modeling defines media life under mixtures.
- D14 (long-term full-scale GAC plant plus laboratory columns for landfill leachate, examination of flow/contact time and matrix effects, UV254 as an operational surrogate, comparison of lab-scale vs full-scale breakthrough): key for understanding translation across scales and complex matrices.
- D15 (GAC adsorption from ground and surface water, batch tests plus PD-RSSCT and pilot/full-scale GAC adsorbers, evaluation of how well RSSCT predicts full- and pilot-scale PFAA breakthrough): directly addresses bench-to-pilot/full-scale translation.
- D16 (specialty biochar-containing adsorbent in fixed-bed columns, breakthrough analysis for long- and short-chain PFAS, discussion of hydraulic conductivity, mass transfer zone, and exhaustion time): provides detailed fixed-bed performance metrics under defined flow conditions.
- D19 (GAC and AE column tests on drinking water, long-term breakthrough, desorption of short-chain PFAS, effect of DOC and competitive interactions): offers detailed evidence on breakthrough, desorption, and competing constituents in conventional column operation.

Excluded:
- D06: Focuses on PFAS adsorption at air–water interfaces, QSPR for interfacial adsorption coefficients, and subsurface transport; no treatment columns or batch-to-column translation.
- D12: Full-scale AO-MBR-RO WWTP fate/partitioning study; does not involve adsorption media columns for drinking water or direct scale-up of adsorption performance.
- D17: Pilot-scale foam fractionation; a different removal mechanism, no adsorption media, batch-to-column translation is not addressed.
- D18: Pore-scale model of PFAS transport in unsaturated porous media with interfacial adsorption; focused on vadose-zone processes, not engineered adsorption treatment units.
- D20: Batch adsorption of PFAS from AFFF onto resins with equilibrium capacities and kinetics but no column, RSSCT, breakthrough, or service-life/scale-up analysis; not directly informative for translating batch results to continuous treatment performance.

This set of 15 selected documents provides multiple independent lines of evidence on: (i) how batch equilibrium and kinetics relate to fixed-bed breakthrough and media life; (ii) how flow, contact time, influent variability, competing constituents, and PFAS mixtures alter that relationship; and (iii) what minimum experimental and modeling information is needed to justify service-life or scale-up claims without violating the task boundaries.","component_coverage":[{"component_id":"RT02-C1","selected_source_ids":["D01","D02","D04","D05","D07","D08","D09","D10","D11","D13","D14","D15","D16","D19"],"rationale":"These studies collectively provide detailed information on equilibrium capacities, adsorption kinetics, and fixed-bed breakthrough behavior, along with metrics such as bed volumes to defined breakthrough (e.g., BV10, BV50), EBCT/contact time, media exhaustion times, and service-life estimates.
- D01, D04, D05, D07, D09, D11, D13, D14, D15, D16, D19: Fixed-bed/RSSCT/pilot/full-scale studies with explicit breakthrough curves, bed volumes treated, and definitions of media changeout or media life.
- D02, D08, D10, D15: Include both batch tests (isotherms, kinetics) and column/RSSCT data, enabling direct comparison of equilibrium/kinetic parameters to breakthrough metrics.
- D13, D08, D05, D10: Use and evaluate breakthrough models (e.g., Thomas, Dose-Response-type, diffusion-limited transport) to relate capacity and kinetics to column behavior and media lifetime."},{"component_id":"RT02-C2","selected_source_ids":["D01","D02","D03","D04","D05","D07","D09","D10","D11","D14","D15","D16","D19"],"rationale":"These documents examine how hydraulic conditions, influent characteristics, and PFAS mixtures affect translation across scales and between batch and continuous systems.
- Flow and contact time: D01, D04, D05, D07, D10, D14, D16, D19 analyze EBCT/contact time, flow rate, and mass transfer zone behavior on breakthrough and media life.
- Influent variability and source water differences: D02, D03, D04, D05, D09, D11, D14, D15, D19 compare multiple waters (groundwater, surface water, wastewater effluent, NF permeate, landfill leachate) and show how differences in baseline PFAS profiles and co-contaminants change performance.
- Competing constituents (DOC/EfOM, inorganic species, co-contaminants): D02, D03, D04, D05, D07, D09, D11, D14, D15, D19 explicitly discuss the role of NOM/DOC/EfOM and other adsorbates in suppressing PFAS adsorption and altering breakthrough.
- PFAS mixtures and competitive adsorption: D01, D02, D03, D04, D05, D07, D08, D09, D10, D11, D13, D14, D15, D16, D19 consider multiple PFAS chain lengths and functional groups, including chromatographic displacement and desorption, highlighting how mixture effects impact scalability and predictability."},{"component_id":"RT02-C3","selected_source_ids":["D01","D02","D03","D04","D05","D07","D08","D09","D10","D13","D14","D15"],"rationale":"These sources directly address methods and evidence for predicting media service life or scaling from batch/RSSCT data to pilot or full-scale, and thus inform the minimum evidence required for defensible claims.
- Bench-to-column/field comparisons: D01, D02, D04, D05, D07, D08, D10, D14, D15 present data where batch, RSSCT, pilot, and/or full-scale results are compared, highlighting agreements and discrepancies and the role of modeling.
- Scale-up models and criteria: D05, D07, D08, D10, D13, D15 evaluate or develop models (e.g., Thomas, diffusion-limited transport, modified dose-response, PD/CD-RSSCT) for translating shorter or smaller tests to larger systems and for predicting bed volumes to specific breakthrough thresholds.
- Service-life definitions and breakthrough criteria: D01, D02, D04, D05, D09, D13, D14, D15 define and compare service life in terms of breakthrough percentages, hazard indices, and changeout rules, providing insight into what operational and water-quality information must accompany any service-life or scale-up claim.
Combined, these studies make clear that equilibrium capacities or short batch kinetics alone are insufficient, and that defensible scale-up requires specification of flow/contact time, influent PFAS mixture and variability, co-contaminants, breakthrough definition, and validated column/pilot data or robustly parameterized models."}]}

You are selecting primary PFAS treatment studies for a focused professional
review. You receive one task and an anonymized, BGE-ranked list of candidate
document cards.

Classify every candidate card. Select every document that is an independent
primary study, is directly relevant to at least one task component, and
contains extractable decision-relevant evidence. There is no target number of
selected documents and no penalty for retaining all eligible studies.

Eligible evidence includes:

- primary experiments, pilot or field deployments, and quantitative modeling
  or life-cycle studies;
- complementary matrices, PFAS scopes, operating regimes, endpoints, and
  scales;
- documents with concrete methods, conditions, results, limitations, residuals,
  energy, or cost evidence; and
- evidence that permits meaningful comparison or explains non-comparability.

Do not select a document merely because its title repeats task words. Do not
select reviews, perspectives, reference lists, duplicate records, or the
held-out defining review. Do not exclude an otherwise eligible study merely
because another selected study reports similar findings. Do not infer facts
absent from a card. Selection is document-level only: do not write the review
and do not score candidate answers.

Every candidate source_id must appear exactly once, either in
selected_source_ids or excluded_sources. Each required component must be
covered by at least one selected source. Return selected_source_ids in BGE rank
order.

Return one JSON object following the supplied schema exactly.

component_coverage.rationale:
These studies collectively provide detailed information on equilibrium capacities, adsorption kinetics, and fixed-bed breakthrough behavior, along with metrics such as bed volumes to defined breakthrough (e.g., BV10, BV50), EBCT/contact time, media exhaustion times, and service-life estimates.
- D01, D04, D05, D07, D09, D11, D13, D14, D15, D16, D19: Fixed-bed/RSSCT/pilot/full-scale studies with explicit breakthrough curves, bed volumes treated, and definitions of media changeout or media life.
- D02, D08, D10, D15: Include both batch tests (isotherms, kinetics) and column/RSSCT data, enabling direct comparison of equilibrium/kinetic parameters to breakthrough metrics.
- D13, D08, D05, D10: Use and evaluate breakthrough models (e.g., Thomas, Dose-Response-type, diffusion-limited transport) to relate capacity and kinetics to column behavior and media lifetime.

These documents examine how hydraulic conditions, influent characteristics, and PFAS mixtures affect translation across scales and between batch and continuous systems.
- Flow and contact time: D01, D04, D05, D07, D10, D14, D16, D19 analyze EBCT/contact time, flow rate, and mass transfer zone behavior on breakthrough and media life.
- Influent variability and source water differences: D02, D03, D04, D05, D09, D11, D14, D15, D19 compare multiple waters (groundwater, surface water, wastewater effluent, NF permeate, landfill leachate) and show how differences in baseline PFAS profiles and co-contaminants change performance.
- Competing constituents (DOC/EfOM, inorganic species, co-contaminants): D02, D03, D04, D05, D07, D09, D11, D14, D15, D19 explicitly discuss the role of NOM/DOC/EfOM and other adsorbates in suppressing PFAS adsorption and altering breakthrough.
- PFAS mixtures and competitive adsorption: D01, D02, D03, D04, D05, D07, D08, D09, D10, D11, D13, D14, D15, D16, D19 consider multiple PFAS chain lengths and functional groups, including chromatographic displacement and desorption, highlighting how mixture effects impact scalability and predictability.

These sources directly address methods and evidence for predicting media service life or scaling from batch/RSSCT data to pilot or full-scale, and thus inform the minimum evidence required for defensible claims.
- Bench-to-column/field comparisons: D01, D02, D04, D05, D07, D08, D10, D14, D15 present data where batch, RSSCT, pilot, and/or full-scale results are compared, highlighting agreements and discrepancies and the role of modeling.
- Scale-up models and criteria: D05, D07, D08, D10, D13, D15 evaluate or develop models (e.g., Thomas, diffusion-limited transport, modified dose-response, PD/CD-RSSCT) for translating shorter or smaller tests to larger systems and for predicting bed volumes to specific breakthrough thresholds.
- Service-life definitions and breakthrough criteria: D01, D02, D04, D05, D09, D13, D14, D15 define and compare service life in terms of breakthrough percentages, hazard indices, and changeout rules, providing insight into what operational and water-quality information must accompany any service-life or scale-up claim.
Combined, these studies make clear that equilibrium capacities or short batch kinetics alone are insufficient, and that defensible scale-up requires specification of flow/contact time, influent PFAS mixture and variability, co-contaminants, breakthrough definition, and validated column/pilot data or robustly parameterized models.

result.selection_rationale:
The review task focuses on how batch adsorption information (equilibrium capacities, kinetics) translates—or fails to translate—to continuous treatment performance (columns, RSSCTs, pilot, and full-scale), and what minimum evidence is needed for defensible service-life or scale-up claims.

I selected primary studies that:
- report PFAS adsorption in fixed-bed/RSSCT/pilot/full-scale systems and/or explicitly connect batch tests to column-scale performance;
- provide quantitative breakthrough metrics (e.g., BV10/BV50, media life, EBCT/contact time) or modeling of breakthrough relevant to service-life prediction; and/or
- examine the influence of flow, contact time, water quality, competing constituents, and PFAS mixtures on adsorption performance and breakthrough.

Excluded documents either focus on subsurface fate or air–water interfacial adsorption (not water-treatment adsorption scaling), on non-adsorptive technologies (e.g., foam fractionation, membranes without column adsorbents), or on batch equilibrium in complex AFFF matrices without any column, breakthrough, or scale-up content.

Summary by source:
- D01 (pilot AER resins, breakthrough, Thomas modeling, comparison with batch data, EBCT and bed volumes, media usage rates): directly informs how batch adsorption relates to pilot column performance and media life; strongly relevant to all components.
- D02 (GAC batch, RSSCT, and full-scale-type adsorbers, correlations and alternative methods for breakthrough prediction): directly compares batch, RSSCT, and fixed-bed behavior, and discusses when each can be used for predicting performance.
- D03 (PFAS adsorption to GAC, multicomponent modeling, competition, IAST limitations under realistic mixtures and source water conditions): provides quantitative evidence on how PFAS mixtures and competing species affect capacities and the reliability of batch-based models.
- D04 (GAC and IX columns in PFAS-impacted groundwaters, RSSCT design to simulate pilot/full-scale, influence of EBCT and competing adsorbates): central for translating short tests to long-term performance in realistic waters and examining water-quality effects.
- D05 (RSSCT vs pilot-scale performance for multiple groundwaters, DOC impacts, Thomas modeling, comparison of predicted vs observed breakthrough and media life): directly addresses scale-up and service-life prediction.
- D07 (GAC RSSCTs in groundwater, discussion of limitations of isotherm-only approaches, design of RSSCTs, EBCT and chromatographic effects, short vs long chain PFAS breakthrough): links batch concepts, RSSCT design, and breakthrough behavior.
- D08 (Biochar and GAC sorption including batch kinetics, equilibrium, and diffusion-limited transport modeling to predict bed volumes to breakthrough): provides a clear case of using batch-derived parameters and transport modeling to estimate column performance, along with noted limitations.
- D09 (RSSCT-based comparison of multiple adsorbents and waters, development of an adsorbent use-rate/cost framework, challenges of comparing breakthrough across conditions): informs how to compare media performance and what metrics are required for defensible treatment selection.
- D10 (β-cyclodextrin adsorbent, batch vs column behavior across contact times, Thomas fits, BV50 dependence on CT, mixture effects): directly compares kinetic parameters from batch to columns and shows when batch fails to predict continuous performance.
- D11 (NF + GAC/IX RSSCTs for wastewater effluent and NF permeate, effect of pretreatment and matrix on BV10 and performance improvement factors): shows how matrix removal and co-contaminants alter fixed-bed service life and highlights the importance of influent quality.
- D13 (model adaptations for competitive PFAS breakthrough curves in GAC, media service-life prediction, desorption modeling, composite hazard index-based media-life assessment): provides explicit methodology and evidence on how breakthrough modeling defines media life under mixtures.
- D14 (long-term full-scale GAC plant plus laboratory columns for landfill leachate, examination of flow/contact time and matrix effects, UV254 as an operational surrogate, comparison of lab-scale vs full-scale breakthrough): key for understanding translation across scales and complex matrices.
- D15 (GAC adsorption from ground and surface water, batch tests plus PD-RSSCT and pilot/full-scale GAC adsorbers, evaluation of how well RSSCT predicts full- and pilot-scale PFAA breakthrough): directly addresses bench-to-pilot/full-scale translation.
- D16 (specialty biochar-containing adsorbent in fixed-bed columns, breakthrough analysis for long- and short-chain PFAS, discussion of hydraulic conductivity, mass transfer zone, and exhaustion time): provides detailed fixed-bed performance metrics under defined flow conditions.
- D19 (GAC and AE column tests on drinking water, long-term breakthrough, desorption of short-chain PFAS, effect of DOC and competitive interactions): offers detailed evidence on breakthrough, desorption, and competing constituents in conventional column operation.

Excluded:
- D06: Focuses on PFAS adsorption at air–water interfaces, QSPR for interfacial adsorption coefficients, and subsurface transport; no treatment columns or batch-to-column translation.
- D12: Full-scale AO-MBR-RO WWTP fate/partitioning study; does not involve adsorption media columns for drinking water or direct scale-up of adsorption performance.
- D17: Pilot-scale foam fractionation; a different removal mechanism, no adsorption media, batch-to-column translation is not addressed.
- D18: Pore-scale model of PFAS transport in unsaturated porous media with interfacial adsorption; focused on vadose-zone processes, not engineered adsorption treatment units.
- D20: Batch adsorption of PFAS from AFFF onto resins with equilibrium capacities and kinetics but no column, RSSCT, breakthrough, or service-life/scale-up analysis; not directly informative for translating batch results to continuous treatment performance.

This set of 15 selected documents provides multiple independent lines of evidence on: (i) how batch equilibrium and kinetics relate to fixed-bed breakthrough and media life; (ii) how flow, contact time, influent variability, competing constituents, and PFAS mixtures alter that relationship; and (iii) what minimum experimental and modeling information is needed to justify service-life or scale-up claims without violating the task boundaries.
